title: FinBen: A Holistic Financial Benchmark for Large Language Models

task.value: A holistic open-source benchmark evaluating LLMs on 36 datasets spanning 24 financial tasks across seven aspects, including the first evaluation of stock trading.
task.quote: we introduce FinBen, the first extensive open-source evaluation benchmark, including 36 datasets spanning 24 financial tasks, covering seven critical aspects: information extraction (IE), textual analysis, question answering (QA), text generation, risk management, forecasting, and decision-making.

architecture.value: Zero-shot prompting evaluation of LLMs on instruction-formatted datasets; the stock trading task uses the FinMem LLM agent, which has short-, mid-, long-term and reflection memory, with different LLMs as backbones.
architecture.quote: We innovatively introduce the SOTA financial LLM agent FinMem (Yu et al., 2023) to evaluate LLMs on the stock trading task.

data.value: 36 datasets, mostly existing public sets plus new EDTSum, Regulations and FinTrade. FinTrade covers 10 stocks (TSLA, NFLX, AMZN, MSFT, AAPL, GOOG, DIS, GM, NIO, COIN) over one year, with historical prices, news and sentiment.
data.quote: FinTrade: We develop the FinTrade dataset specifically for the stock trading task, incorporating historical stock prices, news, and sentiment data. This dataset is the collection of 10 stocks over one year.

window.value: Only test data is used for evaluation. No specific trading dates are given; FinTrade spans one year.
window.quote: We use only test data for evaluation.

models.value: 15 LLMs: ChatGPT, GPT-4, Gemini Pro, LLaMA2-7B/70B-chat, LLaMA3-8B, ChatGLM3-6B, Baichuan2-6B, InternLM-7B, Falcon-7B, Mixtral 8x7B, Code LLaMA-7B, FinGPT, FinMA-7B, DISC-FinLLM, CFGPT. Trading also used GPT-4o, GPT3.5-Turbo and llama3-70B.
models.quote: We evaluate the zero-shot (from our evaluation) and few-shots (results from previous papers) performance of 15 representative general LLMs and financial LLMs on the FinBen benchmark

baselines.value: For trading: Buy & Hold and the RL methods A2C, PPO and DQN. Non-LLM methods (e.g., LSTM, SLOT, BERT-based models) are reported from prior papers for forecasting and NLP tasks.
baselines.quote: compared to other models, including those using reinforcement learning methods like DQN, PPO, and A2C, which show significantly lower SR and higher MDD.

headline_result.value: Averaged across 10 stocks, GPT-4 trading achieved CR 28.19 ± 25.27%, SR 1.51 ± 1.08 and MD 18.34 ± 9.77%, versus Buy & Hold CR -4.00 ± 22.39% and SR 0.02 ± 0.87.

costs.value: No trading cost assumptions are given. Compute was 16 A100 80G GPUs for about 600 hours, with a total spend of about $51,000 including GPT-4 API costs.
costs.quote: These experiments are exclusively conducted on 16 NVIDIA A100 80G GPUs, taking approximately 600 hours to complete. Including the GPT-4 API costs, the total expenditure amounts to approximately $51,000.

uncertainty.value: Results are the average of three runs. Trading results are reported with 95% confidence intervals across the 10 stocks.
uncertainty.quote: All results via our evaluations are the average of three runs.

leakage_controls.value: For the shared task only, a Data Leakage Test compared train/test perplexity for the top-3 teams. No look-ahead controls are described for the benchmark itself.
leakage_controls.quote: To measure the risk of data leakage from the test set used in training, we introduce the Data Leakage Test (DLT). The DLT calculates the difference in perplexity between the training set and the test set.

limitations.value: Limited dataset sizes; evaluation was capped at the LLaMA 70B model because of compute; tasks use American market data and English text only; potential for misuse.
limitations.quote: Computational constraints limited our evaluation to the LLaMA 70B model, potentially overlooking the capabilities of larger models. Additionally, the tasks are based on American market data and English texts, which may limit the benchmark's applicability to global financial markets.

release.value: All datasets, results and code are released on GitHub (The-FinAI/PIXIU).
release.quote: All datasets, results, and codes are released for the research community11 1 https://github.com/The-FinAI/PIXIU.
